{{Quote|The ''Omega Frost''! Brilliant, Silas&hellip;! It's going to be the ''club'' with which we beat ''Darth Vader'' from the Emperor's favor.|Baron Orman Tagge, to his brother, Dr. Silas Tagge|<ref name="Marvel 32" />}}
The '''Omega Frost''' was a [[Superweapon/Legends|superweapon]] designed by [[Doctor/Legends|Doctor]] [[Silas Tagge/Legends|Silas Tagge]] of the [[Tagge Company/Legends|Tagge Company]] and implemented by the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]] in a failed attempt to destroy the [[Alliance Fleet/Legends|Alliance Fleet]]. The Omega Frost was devised to flash-freeze any [[Water/Legends|moisture]]-containing object&mdash;including a living being&mdash;that happened to be positioned between two strategically placed [[conductor tower]]s; material frozen by the weapon, even metal, subsequently shattered. As almost every substance in [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]] contained some degree of moisture, the weapon could be utilized in any environment, including the [[Vacuum/Legends|vacuum]] of [[Realspace/Legends|space]].

In [[0 ABY/Legends|0 ABY]], [[Baron/Legends|Baron]] [[Orman Tagge/Legends|Orman Tagge]], head of the [[House of Tagge/Legends|House of Tagge]] and brother to Silas Tagge, moved forward with the Omega Frost's production. Establishing a testing facility in the [[Jundland Wastes/Legends|Jundland Wastes]] on arid [[Tatooine/Legends|Tatooine]], the Baron and his brother oversaw a successful trial of the weapon's effects within the [[Planet/Legends|planet's]] [[Desert/Legends|deserts]]; even under the intense heat of the [[Tatoo system/Legends|system's]] [[Tatoo I/Legends|twin]] [[Tatoo II/Legends|suns]], the landscape&mdash;and everything on it&mdash;froze. With the testing complete, the Tagge brothers departed Tatooine for the [[Feriae system]], where they prepared to use the weapon to destroy the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Alliance]] [[Fleet/Legends|Fleet]]. The Imperials had not been the only ones to observe the Tatooine demonstration, however; Rebels [[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker]], [[Han Solo/Legends|Han Solo]], and [[Chewbacca/Legends|Chewbacca]] had almost fallen victim to the Omega Frost themselves and vowed to uncover the Tagges' plans.

The Tagges planned to unleash the Omega Frost on the unsuspecting Alliance Fleet within the [[Feswe Corridor]], using more advanced conductor towers to generate the weapon and flash-freeze the Rebel [[Starship/Legends|ships]]. Skywalker attempted to destroy one of the towers before the Rebel Fleet could fall into the trap, prompting Doctor Tagge to prematurely activate the Omega Frost. The Alliance forces narrowly avoided the effective band of the weapon before Skywalker destroyed the tower and stopped the Omega Frost's generation. With the weapon inactive, the Rebel ships proceeded through the Feswe [[Asteroid/Legends|asteroid]] corridor unmolested, taking the opportunity to [[Battle of the Corridor|destroy]] the Tagges' [[Mining Explorer]] and an [[General Tagge's battlecruiser|Imperial battlecruiser]]. The engagement put an end to the Omega Frost, though a conceptual cousin, the [[Metal-Crystal Phase Shifter]], survived into the [[Time/Legends|time]] of the [[New Republic/Legends|New Republic]] and the [[Galactic Federation of Free Alliances|Galactic Alliance]].

==Description==
{{Quote|I believe it's safe to say that ''nothing'' caught between the conductor towers can ''survive''&mdash;not when we generate the ''Omega Frost'', my dear brother.''"<br />"''You'll be able to ''duplicate'' this success anywhere&hellip; in any ''environment''?''"<br />"''Perhaps not in the heart of a ''nova''. But if it works under ''these'' arid conditions&hellip; I'm confident I can adjust it for ''whatever'' you require.|Dr. Silas Tagge and Baron Orman Tagge, after witnessing a successful test of the Omega Frost|<ref name="Marvel 32" />}}
The Omega Frost was a [[Superweapon/Legends|superweapon]] capable of flash-freezing objects of any size<ref name="Intrigue" />&mdash;including [[Sentience/Legends|sentient]] beings<ref name="Marvel 32" />&mdash;to temperatures below the mark of absolute zero through the use of [[Force field/Legends|force fields]] and electromagnetics.<ref name="Intrigue" /> The weapon was capable of freezing an entire [[Planet/Legends|planet]] and functioning properly in the [[Vacuum/Legends|vacuum]] of [[Realspace/Legends|space]].<ref name="Marvel 34" /> Theoretically, it could even freeze an entire [[Star system/Legends|star system]].<ref name="Intrigue" /> The Omega Frost's effect was generated by two [[conductor tower]]s; when these towers were activated, any object containing [[Water/Legends|moisture]] that happened to fall between both conductors'<ref name="Marvel 33" /> effective band<ref name="Marvel 34" />&mdash;even the terrain&mdash;was instantly frozen. The effect was so powerful that even metal shattered after the freezing process.<ref name="Marvel 33" />

==History==
===Development and testing===
{{Quote|I'm moving in ''secret'', Ulric&hellip; using the House of Tagge's great scientific and commercial resources. With ''you'' to assure continued military cooperation&mdash;we'll have ''revenge''&hellip; and ''more''! It's all coming to ''fruition'', little brother&mdash;on a quiet, unsuspecting backwater world called ''Tatooine''!|Baron Orman Tagge, to his brother, Ulric Tagge|<ref name="Marvel 31" />}}
Conceived by [[Doctor/Legends|Doctor]] [[Silas Tagge/Legends|Silas Tagge]] of the [[Tagge Company/Legends|Tagge Company]], the Omega Frost was Tagge's crowning achievement.<ref name="Intrigue" /> [[Baron/Legends|Baron]] [[Orman Tagge/Legends|Orman Tagge]], head of the [[House of Tagge/Legends|House of Tagge]] and Silas's older brother, planned to use the Frost as a means by which the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]] could destroy the [[Alliance Fleet/Legends|Rebel Fleet]] that had been using the [[Feswe Corridor]] to break the [[Yavin blockade|Imperial blockade]] of [[Yavin 4/Legends|Yavin 4]].<ref name="Marvel 33" /> The Baron believed an effective use of the weapon would curry [[Galactic Emperor/Legends|Emperor]] [[Palpatine/Legends|Palpatine's]] favor, at the same [[Time/Legends|time]] granting Tagge the revenge he desired against the [[Emperor/Legends|Emperor's]] enforcer, [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Darth Vader]]. The Baron included his younger brother, [[General/Legends|General]] [[Ulric Tagge/Legends|Ulric Tagge]] of the [[Imperial Military/Legends|Imperial Military]], in the plot as a means of securing Imperial assistance for the project.<ref name="Marvel 31" />

[[File:TaggeInspects.jpg|thumb|left|250px|Baron Orman Tagge and Dr. Silas Tagge inspect the successful testing of the Omega Frost on Tatooine.]]
Doctor Tagge tasked his older brother with selecting an arid world on which the Omega Frost could be tested. Baron Tagge found many locations that fit his brother's conditions, but only one stood out to him&mdash;Tatooine, a [[Desert/Legends|desert]] planet that happened to be the [[Homeworld/Legends|homeworld]] of a young [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Rebel]] hero named [[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker]], whom the Baron hoped he could lure to Tatooine with word of the project. The Tagges purchased several [[Moisture farm/Legends|moisture farms]] on the planet and set up their headquarters in the rocky hills of the [[Jundland Wastes/Legends|Jundland Wastes]], from which they began experimenting with the Omega Frost. One subject, a [[Bantha/Legends|bantha]], managed to escape the facility, but the Omega Frost took effect before long, freezing and [[Death/Legends|killing]] the bantha in its tracks below the heat of the [[Tatoo system/Legends|Tatoo system's]] [[Tatoo I/Legends|twin]] [[Tatoo II/Legends|suns]]. The security breach did not overly concern Baron Tagge, as the project was quickly nearing completion.<ref name="Marvel 31" />

Skywalker did arrive on Tatooine, but for reasons unrelated to the Tagges' secret project. En route to the [[City/Legends|city]] of [[Mos Eisley/Legends|Mos Eisley]] to recruit [[Blockade/Legends|blockade]] runners for the Rebellion, Skywalker happened upon the frozen remains of the escaped bantha in a narrow canyon. An Imperial [[Reconnaissance Troop Transporter]] searching for the creature discovered it at the same time that Skywalker did; the young Rebel managed to avoid detection as a pair of Imperial [[Stormtrooper/Legends|stormtroopers]] proceeded to obliterate the bantha's remains to conceal any evidence of the Omega Frost. Having learned previously that the House of Tagge had bought up moisture [[Farm/Legends|farms]], Skywalker concluded that they were behind the bantha's mysterious death, and he vowed to uncover what exactly was going on.<ref name="Marvel 31" /> The Imperials eventually learned of Skywalker's presence on Tatooine, forcing him to flee with fellow Rebels [[Han Solo/Legends|Han Solo]] and [[Chewbacca/Legends|Chewbacca]] into the desert, where they happened upon the [[Jawa/Legends|Jawa]] crew of a [[Sandcrawler/Legends|sandcrawler]] that aided in their escape.<ref name="Marvel 32" />

Concurrently, the Tagge Company proceeded with their experiments with the Omega Frost. Two conductor towers were established within the Tatooine desert to test the Frost's effect; Skywalker and company discovered both towers when the Jawa crew of the sandcrawler happened upon one of them during their trek. They originally mistook it for a giant [[Moisture vaporator/Legends|moisture vaporator]], but upon closer inspection, Skywalker realized the tower was rapidly getting cold. Remembering the frozen bantha he had stumbled upon earlier, he urged everyone to flee. The three Rebels succeeded in getting the Jawas out of the way before the Omega Frost took effect, but another sandcrawler and its crew were caught between both towers and instantly frozen with the surrounding terrain. Stunned by the field of ice before them, the Rebels and the Jawas watched as the second sandcrawler shattered. A Reconnaissance Troop Transporter arrived on the scene with the Baron and Doctor Tagge aboard; they marveled at the success of the Omega Frost before ordering the capture of the Rebels, who managed to elude the Imperials and flee Tatooine.<ref name="Marvel 32" /> Upon departing Tatooine aboard the [[YT-1300 light freighter/Legends|freighter]] [[Millennium Falcon/Legends|''Millennium Falcon'']], Skywalker and his companions followed Baron Tagge's [[Mining Explorer]] to the planet [[Feriae Junction/Legends|Feriae Junction]], hoping to uncover more details about the weapon they had witnessed.<ref name="Marvel 33" />

===Trap at Junction===
[[File:9super.jpg|thumb|right|250px|Luke Skywalker discovers in the Feswe Corridor one of the conductor towers used to generate the Omega Frost.]]
{{Quote|You see, instead of using the Omega Frost on ''Junction'' as you alerted your ''friends'' to believe&hellip; we're going to activate it ''across'' the corridor. When the Rebel fleet races through here to rescue one of its main sources of ''supplies''&hellip; they're going to be ''destroyed'' by a sudden ''wave'' of the ''ultimate cold''!|Baron Tagge, to Luke Skywalker|<ref name="Marvel 33" />}}
At Feriae Junction, Baron Tagge oversaw the transfer of Omega Frost components to his brother Ulric's [[Tagge battlecruiser|battlecruiser]]. When the ''Millennium Falcon'' arrived in the [[Feriae system]], Skywalker donned [[survival armor]] and slipped in among the workers handling the cargo transfer. Eavesdropping on the [[Comlink/Legends|comm]] chatter, he learned of the Omega Frost's ability to freeze an entire world. Believing Junction&mdash;a key source of supplies to the Rebellion&mdash;to be the target, Skywalker contacted the ''Falcon'' and told Solo to warn the Alliance about the impending use of the weapon; before Skywalker could flee, he was [[Stun/Legends|stunned]] by Imperial stormtroopers and was brought aboard Tagge's Mining Explorer. The Baron revealed the details of his plan to the captive Skywalker; rather than freeze Junction with the Omega Frost, Tagge revealed, the weapon was intended to destroy the Alliance [[Fleet/Legends|Fleet]] as it journeyed through the Feswe Corridor. Skywalker was able to overcome the Baron in a brief [[Lightsaber duel/Legends|lightsaber duel]] before escaping the Mining Explorer in a [[TIE/ln space superiority starfighter/Legends|TIE fighter]] that had been covertly rigged by Doctor Tagge.<ref name="Marvel 33" />

As Skywalker fled, two conductor towers&mdash;substantially larger than the two used on Tatooine, and possessing a far greater range&mdash;were installed on [[Asteroid/Legends|asteroids]] at opposite ends of the corridor in preparation for the Alliance Fleet's arrival.<ref name="Marvel 33" /> The Tagge Mining Explorer detected the approaching fleet on its long-range [[scanner]]s as it moved away from the target zone. When the fleet was midway into the corridor, Doctor Tagge planned to activate the Omega Frost and immediately freeze the Rebel [[Starship/Legends|ships]] and their crews. Skywalker, meanwhile, decided to do whatever he could to prevent the Tagges from fulfilling their plans. Having abandoned his doomed [[TIE series/Legends|TIE]] [[Starfighter/Legends|fighter]], Skywalker used the [[Jetpack/Legends|jetpack]] built in to his survival suit to navigate the asteroid corridor, searching for one of the conductor towers. He arrived at the first of the towers and attempted to destroy it with his [[Lightsaber/Legends|lightsaber]], only to have the attack deflected by the tower's [[Force field/Legends|force field]].<ref name="Marvel 34" />

Skywalker's move prompted Doctor Tagge to activate the Omega Frost prematurely, freezing a large number of asteroids. The Rebel ships were just beyond the weapon's effective band when the Frost activated, however, but as they lacked the maneuverability to avoid the weapon, they would either proceed forward and be frozen, or attempt to turn only to collide with one another. With moments to spare, Skywalker realized that the conductor tower's force field did not extend below the asteroid's surface. He quickly dug into the rock with his lightsaber and slashed at the vulnerable components of the tower beneath the surface. The move shorted out the conductor tower, shutting down the Omega Frost just as the Rebel Fleet pressed forward into the corridor. Stunned by his failure, Doctor Tagge ordered his subordinates to call in reinforcements from his brother, General Ulric Tagge, before rushing out to find the Baron. The Mining Explorer's military liaison officer, [[Lieutenant/Legends|Lieutenant]] [[Shanks]], realized only too late that such a transmission could be detected and pinpointed by the Alliance forces&mdash;the Rebel ships moved in on the Tagges' [[Cruiser/Legends|cruiser]] and [[Battle of the Corridor|destroyed]] it,<ref name="Marvel 34" /> before turning on and destroying [[General Tagge's battlecruiser]].<ref name="Marvel 35">[[Star Wars (1977) 35|''Star Wars'' (1977) 35]]</ref> The battle marked the end of the Omega Frost.<ref name="Marvel 34" />

===Legacy===
Although the Omega Frost weapon's destruction was confirmed by [[Crix Madine/Legends|Crix Madine]], the Rebel general held suspicions that the technology was still out there.<ref name="Imperial Handbook">''[[Star Wars: Imperial Handbook: A Commander's Guide]]''</ref> This suspicion was later confirmed when a conceptual cousin of the Omega Frost<ref name="Homing Beacon">{{HBCite|209}}</ref> known as the [[Metal-Crystal Phase Shifter]] survived into the reign of the [[New Republic/Legends|New Republic]]<ref name="Champions">''[[Champions of the Force]]''</ref> and the [[Galactic Federation of Free Alliances|Galactic Alliance]].<ref name="Revelation">''[[Legacy of the Force: Revelation]]''</ref> The Metal-Crystal Phase Shifter possessed the ability to alter the molecular structure of metal, turning it into a powder.<ref name="Homing Beacon" /> The effects of the weapon were sufficient enough to severely damage the [[Hull/Legends|hull]] of a starship.<ref name="Champions" /><ref name="Revelation" />

==Creators==
===Silas Tagge===
[[File:Silastagge.jpg|thumb|right|150px|Dr. Silas Tagge]]
{{Main|Silas Tagge/Legends}}
{{Quote|I'm a ''scientist''. Having ''invented'' something&hellip; it's logical I should wish to see it ''used''.|Dr. Silas Tagge|<ref name="Marvel 34" />}}
Chief [[Scientist/Legends|scientist]] of the House of Tagge,<ref name="Marvel 34" /> Doctor Silas Tagge was the creator of the Omega Frost, which proved to be his crowning achievement.<ref name="Intrigue" /> Whereas his brother, the Baron, plotted to use the weapon to settle vendettas and secure the Emperor's favor,<ref name="Marvel 31" /> Doctor Tagge was more concerned with ensuring the Omega Frost's success&mdash;though he was not adverse to becoming the next Baron when his brother was temporarily incapacitated.<ref name="Marvel 34" /> He took extra precautions to prevent Luke Skywalker from interfering in his plans,<ref name="Marvel 33" /> but he underestimated the young Rebel's chances. When Skywalker succeeded in shorting out one of the conductor towers, disabling the Omega Frost, Doctor Tagge was stunned by his failure and rushed to awaken his brother, hoping he could remedy the situation. Before anything could be done, the Rebel Fleet destroyed their Mining Explorer.<ref name="Marvel 34" /> Both Tagges narrowly survived the encounter, however, and were placed in [[life support capsule]]s aboard [[Darth/Legends|Darth]] Vader's [[Devastator/Legends|flagship]].<ref name="Marvel 35" />

===Orman Tagge===
[[File:OrmanFace-ALTADigitalV01P448.png|thumb|right|150px|Baron Orman Tagge]]
{{Main|Orman Tagge/Legends}}
{{Quote|Getting ''even'' is one of the great fossil fuels of ''life'', brother Silas. And the hand of ''fate'' in this matter seemed too ''strong'' to resist.|Baron Orman Tagge|<ref name="Marvel 31" />}}
Unlike his scientist brother, Baron Orman Tagge plotted to use the Omega Frost for his own personal gains, using the resources available to him as the head of the House of Tagge to ensure the project met completion. The Baron hoped that a successful demonstration of the weapon would earn him the Emperor's favor, simultaneously fulfilling a vendetta he held against Darth Vader,<ref name="Marvel 31" /> who had blinded him earlier in his life.<ref name="Marvel 33" /> Tagge hoped to eliminate another of his rivals, Luke Skywalker, by drawing him to Tatooine with word of the Omega Frost,<ref name="Marvel 31" /> but the Baron's underestimating of the young Rebel proved disastrous. Skywalker bested Tagge in a brief lightsaber duel, placing the Baron in a state of shock and leaving the fate of the project in his brother Silas's hands.<ref name="Marvel 33" /> Doctor Tagge's personal ambitions got in the way, and as Skywalker disabled the Omega Frost, he rushed to get his comatose brother's assistance. Baron Tagge awoke just as the Rebel ships succeeded in destroying the Mining Explorer.<ref name="Marvel 34" /> He and his brother were recovered by Imperial forces and placed in life support capsules aboard Vader's [[Flagship/Legends|flagship]].<ref name="Marvel 35" /> The Baron later met his end at Skywalker's hands on the planet [[Monastery/Legends|Monastery]].<ref name="Marvel 37">[[Star Wars (1977) 37|''Star Wars'' (1977) 37]]</ref>

==Behind the scenes==
The Omega Frost first appeared in [[Star Wars (1977) 31|''Return to Tatooine'']], issue 31 of the [[Star Wars (1977)|''Marvel Star Wars'']] line of [[Star Wars comic books|comics]]. The weapon went on to appear in issues [[Star Wars (1977) 32|32, ''The Jawa Express'']]; [[Star Wars (1977) 33|33, ''Saber Clash'']]; and [[Star Wars (1977) 34|34, ''Thunder in the Stars'']]. The weapon later received entries in ''[[The Complete Star Wars Encyclopedia]]'' and ''[[Galaxy of Intrigue]]''.

In [[2008]], the Omega Frost was featured in issue 209 of [[StarWars.com]]'s biweekly newsletter, the [[Homing Beacon (newsletter)|''Homing Beacon'']]. The reference to the weapon was done in the style of [[Checklist: 10 Star Wars Superweapons|"Checklist: 10 ''Star Wars'' Superweapons"]], an article that had appeared on StarWars.com only a few days prior. In addition to detailing the origins, functions, and flaws of the Omega Frost, the newsletter also pokes fun at the weapon, comparing it to a gardening tool and claiming it has a "non-draconian" potential for preserving leftovers.
